gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured output for any of the shown chargers. Zelpio's 2 Oct 2026 test with a solar panel tester got 14.75 W in sun and 7.33 W overcast (panel flat) from the SUNER POWER 20W Pro, which is about 74% and 37% of its 20 W rating. In the same test, three other 20 W maintainers kept charging past 15.5 V on an already overcharged battery.
standout_why: I opened three pages ChatGPT got. energyforthetaking.com (27 Oct 2026) says it verified specs against maker and Amazon listings and did no testing. Its SUNER 20W Pro figure of 'around 1.4 amps in peak sun' is the author's own estimate, and Zelpio's measured 14.75 W works out to about 1.1 A at 13 V. solarbatteryscout.com says 'we haven't used these products' and that its articles are AI-generated, and it gives no measured figures. The SUNER, OptiMate and manuals.plus results are maker specs and manuals only. The gopowersolar.com blog redirected, and I did not fetch it after the redirect. None of these pages gives a measured watt, amp or float-voltage figure, or says who measured it.
decides: It doesn't settle the pick because only one of ChatGPT's candidates, the SUNER 20W Pro, has a published measurement. It does show that a '20 W' maintainer gives about 15 W in good sun and about 7 W under cloud. That supports ChatGPT's advice to buy 20 W rather than 10 W for a car stored long-term, and it means 'built-in controller' alone is not enough. Zelpio found several 20 W units that never stopped charging on an overcharged battery. The page should push buyers toward a controller with a stated cutoff voltage, and the SUNER 20W Pro is the only candidate with a measured output on record.

findings.product: SUNER POWER 20W Solar Battery Charger & Maintainer Pro
findings.label: Measured output, overcast, panel flat
findings.note: Zelpio, published and updated 10/2/2026, no named author. Zelpio says each unit was measured with 'a solar panel tester' around midday, first lying flat and then tilted to 28°, under both overcast skies and full sun. Zelpio called this 'above average.' 7.33 W is 37% of the 20 W rating, or about 0.56 A at 13 V (my arithmetic).

findings.product: SUNER POWER 20W Solar Battery Charger & Maintainer Pro
findings.label: Measured output, sun
findings.note: Same Zelpio test. 14.75 W is 74% of the 20 W rating, or about 1.1 A at 13 V (my arithmetic). energyforthetaking.com's untested estimate of 'around 1.4 amps' is higher than this. Zelpio also says the unit survived its 4 ft drop test with a socket extension.

findings.product: SUNER POWER 20W Solar Battery Charger & Maintainer Pro

findings.value: 4.59 lb (heaviest 20 W unit in the test)
findings.note: Zelpio gives the price as 'around $86'. That is Zelpio's figure from 2 Oct 2026, not a maker-store price.

findings.label: Highest measured output among 14 solar battery chargers (Zelpio test)
findings.value: 21.52 W (Flex Solar 20W, hot sunny day); Volt Hero 20W 15.55 W in full sun; Hoy 20W 16.49 W in sun
findings.note: Same Zelpio test. It shows that 20 W-rated units range from about 14 W to 21.5 W in sun. Some brand spellings in the article look phonetic, such as 'Soul Perk' for SOLPERK.

findings.label: Overcharge cutoff failures measured on an overcharged battery (Zelpio test)
findings.value: TBR 20W kept charging at 15.5 V; Shashuing 30W never stopped at 15.5 V; Hoy 20W overcharged to 16.2 V; New Power 20W went 'well past 15' V; Pulseek 12W never cut out at 15.5 V. Units that did cut out: Grestle 25W 13.3/14.1 V, Volt Hero 20W 13.1/14.1 V, NX 20W 13.8/14.5 V, EBL 25W 12.6/13.8 V, Toga Power 13.8/14.5 V (cut-in/cutout)
findings.note: Zelpio connected each charger to a nearly dead battery and to an overcharged battery and recorded where the controller turned charging on and off. It did not report float voltages for the SUNER 20W Pro.

findings.source_title: Auto Express – Best solar chargers for car batteries 2026
findings.note: Tom Barnard, dated 22 Oct 2024 on a URL labeled 2026. Each panel was connected to a multimeter in natural sunlight, sunny and overcast. Auto Express publishes no numbers: it says the OptiMate 'was certainly able to lift the level on some half-flat cells' rather than only maintaining them, and calls its price (around £165) 'eye-watering.' UK test.

findings.note: Tom Barnard, 14 May 2021. Each charger was connected to a discharged but not dead battery in direct sunlight. Hagerty publishes no amp or watt figures. This is the earlier Solar 20W, not the DUO.

findings.product: SUNER POWER 12W Solar Battery Charger Maintainer
findings.label: Battery resting voltage after six months as the only maintainer (Pwice)
findings.note: Byline 'Henry', dated 20 July 2026. The test was on a boat battery left unattended for six months, and the page doesn't say what meter was used.
